newsitem.title: USA: Talbott visits Moscow to discuss NATO.
newsitem.headline: Talbott visits Moscow to discuss NATO.

text.p: Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott and Vice President Al Gore's chief foreign policy adviser left Washington on Tuesday for talks in Moscow this week on NATO and other issues, U.S. officials said.
The visit by Talbott and Gore's adviser, Leon Fuerth, is intended to prepare for a meeting in Washington on Feb. 5-8 between Gore and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
Talbott discussed NATO issues on a trip to London, Paris and Bonn last week.
Gore and Chernomyrdin meet frequently as the Gore-Chernomyrdin commission, which has become a major bilateral channel between the United States and Russia.

But with the United States and its allies in intensive negotiations with Moscow over plans for NATO enlargement and Russia's role in post-Cold War Europe, the Gore-Chernomyrdin talks have taken on new importance.
Senior U.S. officials say the vice president and prime minister recently were empowered by their presidents to deal with the NATO enlargement issue, a role they did not have previously.
"It's a positive devlopment that President (Boris) Yeltsin has authorised Chernomyrdin to roll up his sleeves and work on the problem with Vice President Gore," one senior U.S. official told Reuters.

Talbott's visit follows talks in Moscow on Monday between Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary General Javier Solana, who is negotiating for the allies on terms of a European security-related deal between the alliance and Moscow.
Talbott was expected to arrive in Moscow on Tuesday and begin formal meetings on Wednesday.
